topics.label: Welcome and Lecture Framing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the fifth lecture of the Cancer Biology series and outlines the upcoming themes on cancer evolution, the microenvironment, and cells of origin.

topics.label: Clonal Evolution and Epigenetic Dynamics
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how somatic driver mutations and non-mutational epigenetic alterations drive clonal selection and confer competitive fitness advantages during cancer development.

topics.label: Cell of Origin and Cancer Stem Cell Models
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the role of normal stem cell hierarchies and evaluate experimental evidence for cancer stem cell models in leukemia and colorectal cancer.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and Inflammatory Tumor Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: They demonstrate how chronic inflammation and environmental stimuli act as promoters that cooperate with oncogenic mutations to activate stem-like programs and drive tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Established Tumor Microenvironment, Spatial Profiling, and Evolutionary Synthesis
topics.groupedBecause: They examine stromal dependencies in established tumors, the spatial sequencing technologies used to profile these cellular interactions, and synthesize the multi-factorial coevolutionary model of cancer progression.

topics.label: Closing Remarks and Next Lecture
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and previews the upcoming lecture on cancer therapy.
